# Results — Study 451 (Marubozu)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
full-bodied, wickless candle signals decisive one-way pressure that continues: buy the bullish
marubozu** — encoded as a mechanical rule. A bullish marubozu is an up-bar (close > open) whose
real body fills **≥ 95%** of the high-low range and whose upper and lower wicks are each
**≤ 2%** of the range. The signal is read on the close of *t* (the bar's own OHLC, fully known);
a long is entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward
5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **73** mechanical bullish-marubozu signals pooled across the 5 tapes (body ≥ 95%, wicks ≤ 2%) |
| Timing / costs | signal on the close of *t* (own OHLC, no look-ahead); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument event study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

> **A note on rarity.** A true wickless marubozu is *rare* on adjusted daily ETF bars — only
> **73** fire across 5 tapes over 21 years. That small sample is itself part of the story: the
> pattern proponents draw all day rarely exists at the strict definition, and where it does, it
> does not forecast.

## The signal — bullish marubozu vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch marubozu-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = marubozu − random.

| horizon | n | marubozu | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (maru−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 73 | +6.4 bps  | 58% | +0.22 | +46.6 bps  | **−40.2 bps** | +4.4 bps  | −1.37 | 0.172 |
| 10-day | 73 | −3.2 bps  | 52% | −0.08 | +27.8 bps  | **−31.1 bps** | −5.2 bps  | −0.72 | 0.470 |
| 20-day | 73 | +10.4 bps | 62% | +0.14 | +54.5 bps  | **−44.1 bps** | +8.4 bps  | −0.57 | 0.570 |
| 60-day | 71 | +30.0 bps | 56% | +0.27 | +103.3 bps | **−73.3 bps** | +28.0 bps | −0.64 | 0.521 |

Read it carefully. Even the **one-sample** *t* against zero is flat here (**+0.27** at best) —
the marubozu doesn't even pick up the usual beta convincingly, because there are so few of them.
Against the **drift-matched random baseline** the bullish marubozu is *worse at every horizon*
(Δ = −40.2 / −31.1 / −44.1 / −73.3 bps): a wickless up-day is followed by **less** continuation
than a coin-flip entry. The marubozu-minus-random Welch *t* is **negative at every horizon** and
never remotely clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar. The marubozu does not forecast continuation.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent edge

| ticker | entries | marubozu | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (maru−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 19 | +12.2 bps  | +0.10 | +59.2 bps  | **−47.0 bps**  |
| QQQ | 14 | −59.5 bps  | −0.31 | +116.2 bps | **−175.7 bps** |
| IWM | 13 | +60.7 bps  | +0.31 | −7.7 bps   | **+68.4 bps**  |
| DIA | 15 | −81.0 bps  | −0.50 | +55.0 bps  | **−136.0 bps** |
| GLD | 12 | +149.0 bps | +1.79 | +50.1 bps  | **+98.9 bps**  |

Two names (IWM, GLD) post a positive delta on a dozen-odd trades each; three (SPY, QQQ, DIA) are
sharply negative. No coherent cross-sectional edge — and the per-ticker samples are tiny
(12–19 trades), the hallmark of noise, not signal.

## Geometry placebo — scramble which days are "wickless", nothing changes

The decisive "does the no-wick body matter?" test: keep the price path and the *number* of
marubozu signals identical, but re-assign the marubozu label to a random permutation of bars, so
the wickless geometry is destroyed while the return marginal is preserved.

| test | observed marubozu 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY body-shuffle | +12.2 bps | **0.788** | 500 |

**79% of label-scrambled "marubozu" sets match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.788). The
wickless body carries no information — random bars labelled "marubozu" do just as well. "The
no-wick body forecasts" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* marubozu-continuation (knob `edge`), the same rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | marubozu | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no continuation) | 87 | +14.7 bps | 46% | +0.29 |
| **0.60** (real planted continuation) | 131 | +932.2 bps | 95% | **+17.86** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted
continuation lights up at *t* = +17.86 with a 95% win-rate (Δ = +390.7 bps vs random). The
detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The bullish marubozu does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (marubozu − random = −40.2 / −31.1 / −44.1 / −73.3 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the marubozu-vs-
  random Welch *t* is **negative at every horizon**, max +0). Even the one-sample *t* against
  zero never clears +0.27 — the pattern is too rare and too unremarkable to carry even the usual
  beta.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift is removed — in fact the
  marubozu *underperforms* a dart at every horizon — and costs only deepen the hole. There are
  only 73 strict marubozus in 21 years across 5 tapes; nothing to trade, nothing to scale.
- **"Does the no-wick body forecast"? — BUSTED.** The body-shuffle placebo leaves the result
  intact (*p* = 0.788): random bars relabelled "marubozu" do as well as the real wickless ones,
  so the no-wick body carries no forecasting information. A marubozu is a vivid *description* of a
  strong day, not a forecast of the next one.
